title: Join a table to the study area

ports.note: The parts come from a study area or a polygon layer: connect one.

ontology.note: The receipt asserts the key column, the declared normalisation and every condition the join met by name, so a reader can see that a part matched only because punctuation was folded. No SHACL shape yet: the conditions are reported as findings rather than refused, because a part with no row is a fact about the data and not a malformed input.

changes.description: Joins to a polygon layer as well as a study area, so a boundary file too large to be one extent can still be joined: Nigeria's 774 LGAs are about 218,000 vertices. What a polygon already holds is kept, so a second join adds a column as a merge on a GeoDataFrame does. Multipolygons stay as published.

evidence.note: Checked against the real transcription and the real boundaries of Snow's South London rather than a fixture: 23 of 32 sub-districts match on the published strings and 32 of 32 after folding punctuation and spacing, and no two names collapse together. Unit checks cover each of the four reported conditions, including two parts of one name both taking a rate. Equality after normalisation is string comparison; nothing here establishes that the normalisation generalises beyond a pair of files whose nine differences are all punctuation, nor that a choropleth of the joined values is a sound reading of them.
